title: test-0057-SCI-PHY-SOUND8
passage: In the quiet town of Shantinagar, residents recently reported strange humming noises coming from a large, solid steel bridge. Many villagers assumed the bridge was silent because it appeared completely motionless to the naked eye. However, local scientists explained that the steel structure was actually undergoing rapid, invisible vibrations caused by wind pressure, which produced the audible hum. To investigate further, the team placed sensors on the bridge. They discovered that sound waves travel significantly faster through the solid steel beams than through the surrounding air, as particles in solids are packed more tightly to transmit energy. The team also warned that constant exposure to this high-frequency noise is not just a nuisance for our ears; it can cause significant stress, sleep deprivation, and high blood pressure in humans. While some residents argued that the sound was harmless because it was not loud enough to be painful, the scientists clarified that even low-intensity, high-frequency sounds can affect our long-term health. They emphasized that sound requires a material medium to travel, meaning that if the bridge were floating in the vacuum of space, no sound would be heard at all, regardless of how much it vibrated.
summary: They found out that sound travels much faster through solid steel beams compared to air. They said that sound needs a material medium to travel, so if a bridge was floating in space, no sound would be heard at all, no matter how much it vibrated.
